gap: No result ChatGPT got states rated load per pound of tripod for the candidates: Peak Design Carbon 7.1 lb/lb, Peak Design Aluminum 5.8, Manfrotto Befree Advanced AS aluminum 5.6 and SIRUI Traveler 5C 4.7. None states the largest camera-and-lens kit each one allows under Finding the Universe's own rule of rated load at least 2× the kit: 10 lb for Peak Design, 9.9 lb for the Manfrotto and 4.4 lb for the SIRUI 5C.
standout_why: I compared against findingtheuniverse.com/best-travel-tripods (cited). It lists raw weight, height and load for the Peak Design Carbon and Aluminum, among others, but none of the derived ratios. It does state a rule: rated load should be at least twice the heaviest camera and lens. It never turns that rule into a kit limit for each tripod, and it says load ratings 'aren't comparable between brands'. It names a SIRUI pick 'Best Load for the Weight' without giving a figure. I also tried digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-travel-tripod (cited), but the fetch returned only the page title, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer gives weights and folded lengths but no load ratings at all.
decides: This confirms the Peak Design Carbon as the best load for its weight for a DSLR (20 lb ÷ 2.81 lb = 7.1). The Manfrotto Befree Advanced AS aluminum is close in allowed kit weight (9.9 lb vs 10 lb) but weighs 0.74 lb more. The finding counts against Dealectric's own listed SIRUI Traveler 5C for DSLR use. Its 8.8 lb rating allows a 4.4 lb kit under the 2× rule. Nikon lists the D850 body at 915 g (2.02 lb), so that leaves 2.38 lb for a lens. The 5C also reaches only 54.3 in, against 59.45–60 in for the others. Treat the 5C as a light-DSLR or mirrorless pick, not a full-frame DSLR-with-zoom pick.
